ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper part of the figure shows a short nucleotide sequence labeled mRNA, and below it the corresponding translation into amino acids in a protein, such as Met, Pro, Leu, Ala, Arg; the figure also provides a genetic code table, used to match mRNA codons to amino acids. Reasoning: The question asks why the mRNA in the figure is much smaller than the original mRNA initially synthesized in the nucleus. What is initially synthesized in the nucleus is precursor mRNA, which contains exons and non-coding introns. During mRNA processing, splicing occurs, removing introns and joining exons, so the length of the mature mRNA becomes shorter.

method.method_draft: Describe the visual: a short mRNA strand is shown being translated into amino acids, supported by a genetic code table. Then read the question text asking why this mRNA is much smaller than the original mRNA synthesized in the nucleus. Recognize that the original nuclear RNA is pre-mRNA, and mature mRNA becomes smaller during processing because noncoding introns are cut out. Therefore the cause is excision/removal of introns from the mRNA molecule.
